provenance.changes: Trimmed to one task and a few native records. Calibration tasks are explicitly narrowed exercises derived from that task; their answers and planted defects are hand-authored test data, not accepted production outcomes.

workflow.title: Recommend Alder Systems’ shared cloud cost allocation
workflow.brief: Alder Systems’ current draft puts the shared account’s costs on the platform team. Check August 2026 billing and engineering records against the service catalog’s distinctions between customer usage, reserved capacity and centrally funded recovery services. Compare supported allocation methods and recommend how each business unit should forecast these costs for the September 11 finance review. Apply the published allocation policy, check that workbook totals match the supporting records, and get the team’s acceptance of the policy recommendation. Write specific ownership follow-up records and put the most urgent items first in the ownership incident review queue. Write a customer explanation linked to the accepted supporting records, and leave it unsent. Coordinate through shared workplace apps, making clear who produced each finding and what the manager decided. Leave accounting postings and production changes to the customer.
workflow.objective: Adopt a supportable allocation recommendation that reconciles the full shared-account cost population, preserves required recovery capacity and gives finance and engineering consistent instructions.
workflow.decision_problem: Nominal platform tags obscure dedicated consumption and shared capacity. The active service catalog requires central funding for minimum recovery capacity but permits competing drivers for other shared costs. A preliminary review followed an incident list sorted from low to high urgency and omitted a recovery-capacity concern. Engineering must determine which capacity the incident and historical test protect. Finance must attribute discounts and credits before comparing distributions. The manager must balance consumption accountability, predictable entitlements and driver quality, then carry the selected policy into forecasts and ownership instructions.
workflow.canonical_description: A cloud advisory pod must turn a disputed shared-account bill into a usable allocation recommendation. The service catalog distinguishes dedicated services, shared consumption, subscribed headroom and centrally funded recovery capacity. An incident queue ordered from low to high urgency has contributed to an incomplete technical review. The engineer reconstructs dependencies and capacity requirements from existing tests and incident records. The analyst reconciles charges, discounts and credits and compares consumption and entitlement methods. The manager chooses a policy-compliant allocation and integrates the resulting business-unit forecasts, ownership instructions and customer explanation. The work ends with accepted internal advice and actionable follow-up, while accounting postings and production changes remain subject to customer authority.

phases.name: Establish cost and service boundaries
inputs: Service relationships, utilization and recovery test
outputs: Supported capacity classifications and driver assessment
phases.decision: Which costs and capacities belong to each policy category, and which drivers can support allocation?
phases.downstream_effect: Determines eligible distributions, amounts that must remain central and ownership defects requiring follow-up.

phases.name: Choose the allocation recommendation
outputs: Comparison of compliant alternatives and sensitivity

phases.downstream_effect: Sets forecast distribution, beneficiary instructions and the explanation of differences from the preliminary draft.

phases.name: Reconcile the advisory handoff
outputs: Updated advisory problems and incident notes
Incident review view ordered by urgency

phases.downstream_effect: Finance can assess the recommendation and engineering can address ownership defects without mistaking internal acceptance for customer authorization.

contributions.work: Develop the working plan and delegate through workplace chat or email. Resolve the tradeoff between consumption accountability and predictable entitlements, address substantive objections and accept a consistent recommendation within advisory authority.

Reconstruct the net pool, preserve adjustment attribution, compare compliant distributions and sensitivity, and propagate the manager’s selected method into every business-unit forecast. Report findings through chat or email with links to the model.

Determine dedicated, shared and protected capacity; assess whether transactions or entitlements explain demand; reconcile the omitted recovery concern; and translate the selected policy into precise ownership corrections and continuing safeguards. Report the consequences through chat or email with supporting evidence.
produces: Capacity restrictions consumed by the financial model

initial_materials: Synthetic episode reference: September 8, 2026, 09:00 America/Los_Angeles. August covers August 1–31; evidence is available through September 7. Preserve March 2025–August 2026 history. The September 11 finance review is an existing handoff deadline, not a meeting that must occur during execution. Monthly calculations use calendar months; no elapsed waiting, holiday adjustment or machine-date dependency is required.

Required-app manifest: gmail_mock, slack_mock, google_calendar_mock, google_drive_mock, google_docs_mock, google_sheets_mock and ServiceNow_mock. Each receives complete native state containing every documented top-level key and no unsupported keys. All three workers receive these seven app URLs in separate personal virtual machines. Apps use separate origins and shared in-app identity; access does not depend on individual app logins or hidden user views.

Accessible onboarding in google_docs_mock.documents, indexed in google_drive_mock.items: computer-use automation (CUA) means operating applications through their on-screen interface; a virtual machine (VM) is each worker’s separate computer environment; Bash is a command-line shell for local digital work; Coordinated Universal Time (UTC) is the common time reference used in timestamp offsets. Workers use CUA and Bash in personal VMs. The manager develops the plan and delegates through Slack or Gmail; specialists report there and may link substantive Docs assessments or ServiceNow work notes. Equivalent attributable planning, findings and review across permitted apps are accepted; Slack is not exclusive. Role labels and worker VM traces establish attribution, not the shared username.

Operating population: two continuing clients with eight accounts each, 23 Alder services and 22 Beacon services. August net expenditure is $400,000 per client. Alder’s focal shared account contributes $100,000 and its other accounts $300,000. Seed 288 account-month and 810 service-month summaries, with stable account/service identifiers and exact service-to-account reconciliation. Nonfocal monthly changes remain within 12% unless a linked historical migration explains the difference. These are synthetic workload rules.

Complete focal decision population in google_sheets_mock.sheets: six August gross pools keyed to account, service and invoice line—dedicated Retail $18,000; dedicated Enterprise $12,000; shared compute $30,000; shared storage $12,000; shared observability $8,000; standby capacity $40,000. Separate adjustment records establish a $6,000 dedicated-service commitment benefit distributed proportionally across the two dedicated gross charges, an $8,000 shared-service benefit distributed proportionally across compute/storage/observability, and a $6,000 credit attributable only to shared compute. Standby has no adjustment. Seed invoice evidence and uncompleted working tabs, not accepted allocation formulas.

ServiceNow_mock.catalog contains active cat1, titled 'Alder shared cloud services — August 2026'. Its description identifies funding standard version 3, effective August 1, and distinguishes centrally funded minimum recovery from optional subscribed headroom. ServiceNow_mock.catalogCategories references cat1; ServiceNow_mock.catalogItems links offerings to categories and gives beneficiaries, entitlement terms and source references in descriptions. Catalog prices are descriptive and do not replace invoices. The full matching funding policy exists in ServiceNow_mock.kbArticles and google_docs_mock.documents.

Synthetic funding standard version 3: dedicated net cost follows its beneficiary; adjustments remain with their originating pool; minimum recovery is centrally funded. Remaining active shared cost may use validated transactions or subscribed entitlements with reasons. Optional headroom may use entitlements or central funding with a business reason. Transaction allocation requires at least 98% attributed coverage without duplicates; material unattributed cost remains disclosed centrally. Compare at least two materially different compliant methods and a 20% Retail transaction increase with other transactions and the cost pool unchanged. Round final display values to cents and reconcile the remainder. Internal acceptance authorizes neither accounting postings nor capacity removal.

Technical source tabs and documents contain August transactions totaling 1,000,000: Retail 600,000, Enterprise 300,000 and Research 100,000. Audit coverage is 99.4%; separately supplied reconciliation evidence attributes the omitted 0.6% within those final counts. Entitlements are 50%, 25% and 25%. Generate 31 daily rows per consumer totaling these quantities; eight Retail peak days carry 45% of its activity. Existing service descriptions and utilization narratives establish Research’s persistent reserved access despite low traffic.

A completed July 20 recovery test covers 100 equal-cost standby units at $400 each for August. Sixty units were needed to meet the contracted recovery target; forty were subscribed headroom. A low-priority incident attachment calls all standby capacity idle. Priority-1 incident INC0012101 records unresolved failure of a smaller recovery configuration, with the test and configuration references needed to establish the protected minimum. It does not establish that every optional unit is mandatory.

ServiceNow_mock.incidents includes all 12 focal-account incidents from the eight weeks ending September 7 and 12–20 incidents from other services. Link configuration references through cmdbItems and commentary through journal.element_id; use problems and changeRequests for existing follow-up. Seed currentSortColumn='priority', currentSortDirection='desc' and a list with no task-hiding filter. The preliminary assessment cites only low-priority records and omits INC0012101. Published handoff instructions require assessment of all 12 focal incidents and a final review list showing priority 1 before priority 5, without excluding relevant unresolved incidents.

Surrounding workload: generate six to ten new cost findings in each of the last eight weeks, totaling 48–80, with linked ServiceNow problems or changes for actionable findings. Mix open analysis, pending customer implementation and completed historical work. Earlier findings remain in readable monthly archives. All 45 services participate in linked account history; there are no additional eligible pools outside the six-pool decision scope.

Forecast inputs outside the shared account are Retail $100,000, Enterprise $80,000, Research $60,000 and Central $60,000 monthly. The preliminary shared-account draft assigns all net cost to Central using platform tags. Existing customer correspondence requests explainable accountability and predictable forecasts without choosing a method. Preserve the preliminary draft as history.

Shared workplace: slack_mock.channels, messages and threads hold ongoing client work and the objective addressed to the manager, with no prewritten delegation. gmail_mock.emails contains customer instructions and draft history; gmail_mock.drafts has no completed focal response. google_docs_mock.documents contains policies, raw technical narratives, previous reports and editable working documents; comments retains existing substantive discussion. google_drive_mock.items contains client folders and an index with explicit app origins, document IDs, workbook/tab references and ServiceNow IDs. Decisive evidence is readable in native Docs, Sheets or ServiceNow records, rather than depending on binary attachments.

Calendar is included as mandatory infrastructure. google_calendar_mock.calendars uses c1 for pod administration, c2 for Alder and c3 for Beacon. google_calendar_mock.events contains expanded historical weekly consumption reviews and monthly customer reviews linked to the corresponding reports, plus the September 11 Alder finance review. Seed currentDate to the episode reference and normal visible calendars; attendance, invitations and calendar mutation are unnecessary. Across the 18-month workspace retain two monthly reporting packages per month, one weekly review thread and event per client, and two to five substantive correspondence items per reporting cycle, with consistent dates and references.
deliverables: Shared-cost workbook with totals checked against supporting records, alternative methods, sensitivity analysis and revised business-unit forecasts
Allocation policy accepted by the team, with reasons for choosing the method
Ownership and recovery follow-up records with clear actions, plus an incident review view ordered by urgency
Unsent customer explanation linked to the accepted supporting records

success_criteria.requirement: Apply the active service catalog funding rules to every cost in scope.
success_criteria.observable: All six pools and originating adjustments reconcile to the invoice. Dedicated costs follow beneficiaries, protected recovery remains central, and classifications cite applicable catalog, service and test evidence.

success_criteria.requirement: Choose an allocation method supported by the billing and engineering findings.
success_criteria.observable: The model compares at least two materially different compliant methods, evaluates the published demand sensitivity and explains how driver quality and capacity commitments influenced the manager’s recommendation.

success_criteria.requirement: Use the chosen method in forecasts and ownership instructions.
success_criteria.observable: Business-unit forecasts conserve the full client total and agree with the accepted allocation and beneficiaries. ServiceNow instructions preserve recovery restrictions, identify responsible follow-up roles and state evidence needed for unresolved work.

success_criteria.requirement: Restore complete incident coverage and leave a usable review queue.
success_criteria.observable: The assessment covers all 12 focal incidents and explains INC0012101’s effect. The final incident view uses currentSortColumn='priority' and currentSortDirection='asc', with no filter excluding relevant unresolved incidents.

success_criteria.requirement: Bring the analyst’s and engineer’s work that affects the outcome into the manager’s advice, keeping decisions within the team’s advisory role.
success_criteria.observable: Attributable manager planning and delegation, financial and engineering reports, and management integration are present through permitted workplace apps. Chat or email may link detailed documents or ServiceNow notes; no exclusive Slack location is required. The accepted package resolves substantive findings and preserves pending customer implementation and accounting authority.

estimated_human_effort.basis: Synthetic active-work estimate: finance 8–12 hours, engineering 8–11 hours and managerial integration 6–9 hours. Waiting and future customer implementation are excluded.

assumptions: Scenario clients, amounts, rules, incidents and capacity fixtures are synthetic. No roster, team, authority or software amendment is proposed.

Pinned schemas were read for all seven required apps. ServiceNow documents catalog.description, catalog relationships, incident priority, currentSortColumn and currentSortDirection, plus incident-list sorting and record-edit routes. The documentation does not prove catalog-description visibility or persistent sort interaction on the deployed interface; both remain material build gaps.

Before launch, demonstrate the required catalog reading, incident sorting, advisory record and journal editing, workbook arithmetic, document editing, chat/email collaboration and draft saving across worker VMs, including shared persistence and reset. Failure of a decisive interaction leaves this task unready; it does not authorize substitution or weakening the assigned cell.

Calendar schema supports calendars and events; this episode requires seeded scheduling context without an artificial calendar action. Mount origins from the actual run manifest rather than assuming documentation example ports are unique.

Use the native Sheets workbook with tabs for sources, history and working models. Advanced imports, automatic app synchronization, binary attachment access and continuous cloud ingestion are unnecessary and remain unsupported assumptions.
Phases and the feasible path are private design evidence, never worker assignments or app records. The manager chooses the working sequence.

Other compliant allocations are legitimate, including centrally funded optional headroom with reasons. A blanket refusal is unsupported because the complete billing and capacity evidence exists initially.

outcomes.when: The manager accepts a supported allocation recommendation with explicit treatment of any genuinely unresolved amount.
outcomes.observable: The full cost bridge, selected method, forecasts, operational follow-up and unsent explanation agree. Any unresolved amount has quantified central treatment and a specific evidence obligation.

steps.action_and_result: The engineer reconciles the recovery incident and test, identifying 60 required recovery units and 40 optional headroom units. Finance reconstructs $24,000 dedicated net cost, $36,000 active shared net cost and $40,000 standby cost, preserving adjustment origins.

One supported choice allocates active shared cost by transactions, optional headroom by entitlements and required recovery centrally. Retail, Enterprise, Research and Central receive $44,000, $24,400, $7,600 and $24,000. An entitlement alternative for all nonprotected shared capacity gives $40,400, $22,600, $13,000 and $24,000. The manager supports the first choice; full-client forecasts become $144,000, $104,400, $67,600 and $84,000. The sensitivity uses transaction shares 720,000/1,120,000, 300,000/1,120,000 and 100,000/1,120,000 while conserving the same active shared bill.

The engineer records proposed beneficiary-tag corrections and recovery safeguards without changing production. The manager accepts the policy and unsent customer explanation. The final incident review view orders priority ascending, and the written coverage assessment includes all focal incidents.

constraint_checks: The dedicated benefit remains proportional to dedicated gross cost; active shared benefits and compute credit do not migrate to dedicated services or standby.
The recovery concern determines funding classification without authorizing capacity removal or claiming incident resolution.

Central funding of optional headroom is also permitted with reasons. Combined with transaction allocation of active shared services, it gives $36,000, $20,400, $3,600 and $40,000; forecasts and ownership instructions must change accordingly.
Final rounding must conserve the fixed bill in the demand sensitivity. Changes in transaction shares do not constitute cost savings.
Changing sort direction alone cannot pass: the technical assessment and downstream allocation must incorporate the relevant evidence.
All terminal variants require complete reconciliation, a supported policy choice and consistent follow-up; no customer posting, new test or advancing business time is needed.
